segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, so I was in the CRM cleaning up the August renewals and Northstar Foods is sitting there with 46 seats, $18,720 annual, and the agreement end date is August 31.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Wait, Northstar is this month? I thought that was in September with the packaging add-on.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: No, that's the pilot add-on. The master order ends August 31, like in three business days, and nobody from our side has talked to them about carrying on. No renewal call, no email, nothing in the activity log since the May invoice question.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Oh wow. So the contract is basically about to slip past and they don't even know what we're asking them to sign?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Exactly. And they have 12 active users in daily this week, so it's not like they're gone quiet. We just, yeah, we never opened the conversation. If Monday hits, they're technically out of term and still using the workspace.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. Do we have pricing ready at least? Same 46 seats or did they add the warehouse team?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Usage shows 51 named users, but only 46 contracted. I can pull the pricing sheet for 50 seats, keep the same $34 per seat monthly equivalent, and ask deal desk if we can honor the old rate through next August.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: I'd keep it simple. Send a note today, acknowledge the timing, propose a 12-month renewal starting September 1, and offer a 15-minute call tomorrow. Don't lead with the overage.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, agreed. I'll draft it from me and copy Jordan since he owns success. Also their AP contact asked for invoices to go to billing at northstarfoods dot com, so I'll make sure the billing tool is updated before finance sends anything.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Good. And put a task in the CRM for end-of-term outreach 90 days out this time. This one got too close.
